newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican rebels to send woman commander to capital.
newsitem.headline: Mexican rebels to send woman commander to capital.

text.p: Mexico's Zapatista rebels in the southern state of Chiapas won a concession from the government on Wednesday to send their first commander to Mexico City -- a woman leader dying of a terminal illness.

Permission for Commander Ramona to attend an Indian congress in the capital ended a tense stand-off between the two sides. The government had threatened to arrest rebel leaders who left Chiapas to travel to the capital.

Zapatista leader Subcommander Marcos told a news conference in this remote rebel stronghold that after 50 hours of negotiations with peace mediators acting on behalf of the government, the stalemate was broken by the decision to let Ramona attend the forum.

He said it was the Tzotzil woman's "dying wish" to travel to the forum, and would make her the first Zapatista rebel leader to be allowed out of Chiapas since the Indian rebel army rose up against the government on Jan. 1, 1994.
Originally, other rebel leaders such as Marcos had been invited to attend the forum, but the government forbade it and the two sides had been at loggerheads since.
